source_row.english: The following selections are from the Great Book on the Steps of the Path, composed by Je Tsongkapa (1357-1419).

spans.rationale: The complete author name is explicitly attested. Dates remain outside the name because they have no Tibetan source characters here.
Honorific/name member is the printed Je within the complete author name. It is not the title adjective Great.
The personal-name member is unique and strictly tighter inside Je Tsongkapa.
Standalone agentive GIS marks the author of the composition and is rendered by. No detached suffix is used.

The complete source spelling is supported by full BRTSOMS PA records with compose/composed senses. Preserve this form; neither a different tense paradigm nor a spelling preference warrants correction.

spans.eng: Great Book on the Steps of the Path
spans.complete_local_clause_anchor: Great Book on the Steps of the Path
spans.rationale: The complete established work title has this exact translated title in the full lexical evidence. Do not align the author honorific MCHOG to the title Great.
The path member belongs inside the book title, with its printed capital letter.
The steps member is unique inside the title; preserve GMR Steps, without substituting stages.
The great member is unique and strictly tighter inside the title. Book remains part of the whole title rather than being forced onto MO or another absent noun.
Final LAS is the source/ablative relation from this book, not the action noun used in364.

omissions.reason: The additional supreme honorific has no separate certain English exponent. Je already belongs to RJE, and Great belongs to CHEN MO in the book title; broader honorific/name interpretation remains possible, so MCHOG is omitted rather than marked absent. The bound attribution/genitive ending is not split into a separate English word.

omissions.english: The following selections are; the; on the; of the; (1357-1419)
omissions.reason: Selection framing, articles and supplied dates remain verbatim outside independent spans. Relational title words are covered by the whole established title, without invented Tibetan particle members. Full name records also contain dates, but dictionary context does not create absent Tibetan date characters.
